- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day windows.
- Underestimate when sentiment is neutral or flat (sentiment history = 0.00), suggesting lack of momentum; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with recent trend persistence.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >80.00) — cap forecast peaks at +5% above true peak to avoid overreaction.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment; dampen forecast slope after day 10–15 to reflect diminishing momentum.
- If sentiment history is all 0.00, assume no directional bias — use only historical mean and volatility to anchor forecast, avoid trend extrapolation.
